solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Altered borders ultimately all will be disputed (10)

indicatorNotes.borders: as a verb, to border something is to run along its edges, so CHANGED sits on both sides of the other letters
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means at the end, so each word gives up its final letter

blocks.note: last letters of alL, wilL, bE

annotation.surface: Someone complains that the borders were redrawn and every one of them will now be contested.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borders' looks like a noun about frontiers; here it is a verb, CHANGED going around the other letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a result or claim that someone has contested has been called into question.

entries.clue: I approve this location for those attending more than once (4,4)

indicatorNotes.for those attending: to attend can mean to listen, so those attending are the listeners, and the word is given as they receive it
indicatorNotes.more than once: the phrase is to be said again, so the same sound appears twice in a row

annotation.surface: A note about a venue that suits people who come back repeatedly.
annotation.walkthrough: HEAR HEAR is what members of the British Parliament call out to back a speaker. 'Those attending' sounds like visitors, but it means listeners.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the cry is a spoken show of agreement from an audience, standing for the speaker's own 'I approve'.

entries.clue: Pound sheltering a dog (3)

indicatorNotes.sheltering: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so the pound symbol keeps A within it

blocks.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

annotation.surface: A dogs' home takes in a stray.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pound is an animal shelter; the wordplay wants the weight, LB. The A inside the pound does double duty in the definition 'a dog'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the everyday short name for the Labrador retriever, one breed of dog.

entries.clue: Guard at gate failing to open gate, perhaps (5)

indicatorNotes.failing to open: the opening of a word is its first letter, and failing to have it means that letter goes

blocks.note: a soldier posted on guard; lose its first letter
surface padding: says where the guard stands

annotation.surface: A gatekeeper cannot get the gate to open.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failing to open' reads as a stuck gate, but it tells you to remove the S from SENTRY.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a gate is one kind of way in, hence 'perhaps'.

entries.clue: Book group? (7)

blocks.note: the first book of the Bible

annotation.surface: A book club, or someone asking for a book group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book group' sounds like a reading circle; split it and each word is its own definition of the same name.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the opening book of the Old Testament, and the rock band of Phil Collins and Peter Gabriel.

entries.clue: In France, some bother nabbing a reckless criminal (9)

indicatorNotes.In France: the word wanted is the one a French speaker would use for 'some'
indicatorNotes.nabbing: to nab is to grab, so the bother takes hold of the next piece and keeps it right against itself

blocks.note: a = per, as in ten pounds a head

annotation.surface: A French police report: a spot of trouble ends in the arrest of a dangerous outlaw.
annotation.walkthrough: The easy thing to miss is A = PER, from prices like 'two pounds a kilo'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Spanish, familiar from Westerns: a bold, violent outlaw with nothing to lose.

entries.clue: Some people have returned to lend a hand (4)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the words are used
indicatorNotes.returned: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the last three letters of 'people' and the first of 'have'

annotation.surface: Some people have come back to pitch in.
annotation.walkthrough: The run of letters spans the gap between two words, which is where hidden answers usually sit.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: lending a hand is the everyday phrase for assisting someone.

entries.clue: Odd demand shown for used gear (4-2-5)

indicatorNotes.Odd: odd means strange, and a strange arrangement of the letters is what is wanted

annotation.surface: A strange request has been made for second-hand equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like it might mean odd letters, but the count shows DEMAND SHOWN is exactly the 11 letters needed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: clothes or kit passed down from an older sibling or earlier owner, so already used.

entries.clue: Reduced stuff written on some dull list (6)

indicatorNotes.Reduced: reduced means cut down, so the word is shortened to its usual abbreviation
indicatorNotes.on: in a down answer, one piece written on another sits above it

blocks.note: stuff written = literature, shortened to LIT

annotation.surface: Cut-down notes jotted onto a boring list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' reads as describing a shortened list; it belongs to 'stuff written', trimming literature to LIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: originally a church prayer of repeated petitions, now any long, tedious recital, as in a litany of complaints.

entries.clue: Talk continuously, except about potentially boring thing taking place (6,2)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned around, as in 'about turn', so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: bar = except; turned round it is RAB
on = happening, as in 'the match is on'

annotation.surface: Someone talks nonstop, except about something dull happening.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' wants to mean dull; it means making holes, so the thing is a drill BIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in British slang, to rabbit on is to chatter at length without a pause.

entries.clue: Private areas in clubs hosted by one who’s big at present time? (6)

indicatorNotes.hosted by: a host has guests inside their home, so the clubs letter goes inside the other word

blocks.clueFragment: one who’s big at present time?
blocks.note: the big figure at Christmas, present time

annotation.surface: Exclusive rooms at clubs laid on by a local bigwig of the moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present time' reads as 'now', but it means the time of giving presents, so the big figure is SANTA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in Latin plural form: a sanctum is a private room or retreat, and these are several of them.

entries.clue: Particular house in comfortable surroundings (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the house abbreviation goes in the other word
indicatorNotes.surroundings: the comfortable word surrounds the house, wrapping round it on both sides

blocks.note: ho. is the abbreviation for house

annotation.surface: A particular house set in snug grounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is not describing the house; it is the definition, meaning fussy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a particular eater or shopper is hard to please and fussy about what they accept.

entries.clue: Regular contributors to robust old group currently not working (3,2,6)

indicatorNotes.Regular contributors to: letters at regular intervals are the ones contributing, so every other letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a faction is a group within a party

annotation.surface: Stalwart members of a veteran band are not playing at the moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regular contributors' sounds like loyal members of the group; it tells you to take regular letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a machine or player sidelined for now by damage or injury is described this way.

entries.clue: Angry snitch admitting what the Mafia disaffirm in the end (8)

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit is to let in, so SING lets the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.in the end: each word gives up the letter at its end

blocks.note: to sing is to inform on others
last letters of whaT thE mafiA disaffirM

annotation.surface: An informer, furious, confesses what the Mob insist is untrue.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the Mob denying the informer's story; 'in the end' is a mechanical instruction covering four words.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in informal British English, someone steaming is furious, as if boiling over.

entries.clue: Trained seals swimming somewhere in the Pacific (6,6)

indicatorNotes.swimming: things swimming move about freely, so the letters move into a new order

annotation.surface: Circus seals take a swim somewhere out in the Pacific Ocean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trained' looks like the instruction, but it is part of the letters; 'swimming' does the mixing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Chilean island famous for its giant stone heads lies in the south-east Pacific.

entries.clue: Switch behind large stove (9)

blocks.note: a range is a large cooking stove

annotation.surface: A switch placed behind a big cooker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a noun, a light switch by the cooker; it is a verb meaning to swap round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to switch things around is to put them in a different order.

entries.clue: Illegally enter resort breaking lock (8)

indicatorNotes.breaking: something breaking a word splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: a lock of hair is a tress

annotation.surface: A burglar breaks the lock to get into a holiday resort.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface lock is on a door; the wordplay wants a lock of hair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going onto land or into a building without the right to be there.

entries.clue: Ostentatious, pro-conflict Democrat giving glimpse of what’s to come (12)

annotation.surface: A showy, hawkish American politician hints at what lies ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pro-conflict' reads as one word for hawkish; split at the hyphen, each half gives its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from film and fiction: a scene that jumps ahead in time, showing the future.

entries.clue: Important suspect picked up somewhere secret (7)

indicatorNotes.picked up: picked up by the ear, as a radio picks up a signal

annotation.surface: A leading suspect is arrested at a secret location.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' and 'picked up' read as police work; suspect is a verb, and 'picked up' means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a concealed place where fugitives lie low.

entries.clue: Where animals may eat, close to verdant part of golf course (6)

indicatorNotes.close to: a close is an end, so the end letter of the next word is wanted

blocks.note: the rough is the long grass beside the fairway

annotation.surface: Grazing animals feed beside the green part of a golf course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near'; it means the end of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the long open container that farm animals feed or drink from.

entries.clue: Got reminder to take medicine? (8)

indicatorNotes.to take: to take something is to hold it, so the reminder holds the medicine inside it

blocks.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder
a cure is one kind of medicine, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: Someone received a reminder to take their pills.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a pill alarm; the wordplay makes 'take' mean hold inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: obtained or acquired something, often with some effort.

entries.clue: Stop initially doing everything slowly — it’s so thoughtless (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: doing everything slowly — it’s so thoughtless
blocks.note: first letters of Doing Everything Slowly It's So Thoughtless

annotation.surface: A plea to someone to stop dawdling over everything, which is so inconsiderate.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a complete complaint, so the six initials are easy to read past; the dash is only punctuation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in the legal phrase 'cease and desist': to leave off doing something.

entries.clue: Gloomy days are somehow beginning to recede (5)

indicatorNotes.somehow: somehow means in some unstated way, so ARE comes out in some other order
indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Grey days are starting to lift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Days' is not part of the definition; it supplies only its abbreviation D.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary use: a poetic, shortened form of dreary, meaning dismal.

entries.clue: Possible problem for low-level member of British workers’ collective (6)

annotation.surface: A junior member of a British trade union might be trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low-level member' sounds like a junior union member; it is the foot, the body's lowest limb.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a painful swelling at the base of the big toe, trouble for the lowest limb.

entries.clue: Clothing company always primarily protected by patent (8)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of the word is used
indicatorNotes.protected by: whatever is protected is kept inside, so the letters go within the patent word

annotation.surface: A fashion firm whose designs are always covered by patents.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Patent' reads as a legal right; here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a heavy coat worn over other garments is one item of clothing.

entries.clue: Vehicle in speed event almost overturned (3)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short
indicatorNotes.overturned: in a down answer, turned upside down reads backwards

blocks.note: a race, missing its last letter

annotation.surface: A car flipped over during a race.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a crash; 'overturned' is really an instruction to flip the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the motor car is the everyday road vehicle.

entries.clue: Weak article reduced in length (4)

indicatorNotes.reduced in length: a word made shorter loses letters, here just its last one

blocks.note: an article is an object; drop the final G

annotation.surface: A feeble piece of writing has been cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' is not a/an/the here but an object, a thing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an unconvincing excuse or a watery soup lacks strength.

entries.clue: Increase introduced by key power business (10)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: whoever introduces something comes before it, so the other pieces lead and RISE follows

blocks.note: the Enter key on a keyboard

annotation.surface: A rise brought in by a leading energy firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key power business' reads as one phrase about an energy company; it breaks into key, power and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a company or commercial venture.
